hints: The route takes exactly 48 moves, so each step must match its character or use any direction for ?.
Mark visited squares and reject a move outside the board or into a visited square.
Stop a branch early if it splits the remaining unvisited cells into disconnected regions; this avoids counting paths that cannot finish.
analogy: Explore the maze one move at a time, crossing off visited cells and abandoning a route when it seals off an area.
example: A fixed first move up from the upper-left corner is invalid immediately because it leaves the grid.
algorithm: Depth-first search from (0,0), following the specified direction when fixed and all four when ?. Count only paths reaching (6,0) on move 48; prune boundaries, revisits, premature target arrival, and corridor splits.
correctness: Each valid route has one unique sequence of 48 choices explored by DFS; each prune detects a condition that makes completion impossible, so no valid route is removed.
complexity: Worst-case search is exponential, but pruning makes this fixed 7x7 task practical; O(48) recursion and O(49) visited-grid space.
